name: Civil unrest
summary: Police held 154 after Yogyakarta protests on 10 Nov; unrest goes on in Pakistani Kashmir; no nationwide deadly unrest
state: Police in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, used tear gas and water cannon on protesters on 10 Nov and said they detained 154 people (Malay Mail, 11 Nov). In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, AJK police said a Rangers officer injured in firing at a Rawalakot police post on 5 Nov died on 8 Nov; protest groups called for talks and an independent inquiry (Express Tribune, 9 Nov). Searches on 15 Nov found no deadly nationwide unrest or major new crackdown.
for_you: Protests can disrupt transport and close roads at short notice. FCDO travel advice for Indonesia and Pakistan covers demonstrations.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests in several countries and deadly unrest in one (AJK, 5–8 Nov); not nationwide

sources.title: Malay Mail — Indonesia police deploy tear gas, water cannon in Yogyakarta unrest, detain 154
Express Tribune — TTAP calls for immediate end to violence, resumption of talks to quell AJK unrest

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
